messages:
jia: quick question — when we do header-based routing for X-Customer-Tier, do we want the gateway to enforce per-tenant quotas before routing, or route first and let the downstream service apply limits? thinking about dedicated pools vs hosted fallbacks.
andre: route-first risks overwhelming a dedicated pool if quotas are only downstream. i'd lean gateway-enforced quotas, but need a clear exception for reserved dedicated customers.
matt: gateway quota enforcement also lets us emit consistent telemetry and early 429s. downside: gateway has to understand tenancy mapping (tenant header -> quota key). doable via mapping table.
olivia: UX concern: console rollouts. If gateway enforces, the Console needs a clear toggle per-route so SEs can opt out during canary. otherwise we get surprised 429s during rollout.
jia: agreed. proposal: default enforcement at gateway, with a per-route opt-out flag that is rollout-able (canary + audit log). also annotate reason codes so client teams know if it was gateway quota or downstream.
andre: +1. also want metric naming standardized: gateway.quota.rejects.{tenant}.{route}. we should add a telemetry tag for routing_decision={header, ua, signed_assertion}.
telemetry-bot: note: added metric suggestion to the infra board backlog (#infra-telemetry).
matt: config sketch for the rule (WIP):
```
routes:
  - match: header X-Customer-Tier == "premium"
    route_to: dedicated-pool-v2
    quota_enforce: true
    quota_key: tenant_id_header X-Tenant-Id
    enforcement_mode: gateway
    enforcement_exceptions:
      - condition: header X-Bypass-Quota == "true"
        reason: reserved-dedicated
```

olivia: for audit/console: surface when enforcement_exceptions are used, and allow time-limited exceptions from the console (auto-expire). also surface routing_decision in the request trace.
jia: thought about UA-based heuristics — e.g. older sdk versions may not send tenant header reliably. should we fall back to UA inference? that's fuzzy.
andrew: (typo) andre: UA inference is brittle. if we do it, mark as low-confidence and route to a safe default (hosted) and add a telemetry counter for inferred_tenant=true. then schedule an outreach to the SDK owners.
matt: rollout plan: 1) implement gateway quota enforcement + metrics 2) add per-route opt-out flag + console toggle in dark mode 3) run canary with 5% traffic where opt-out=false 4) monitor gateway.quota.rejects & routing_decision tags for anomalies 5) enable gradual ramp.
jia: one more: error payload should include a machine-friendly error_code and human_reason, e.g. {"error":"quota_exceeded", "error_code":"GATEWAY_QUOTA_TENANT", "route_decision":"header"}. makes debugging much easier.
olivia: +1. i'll draft a console UX stub for the toggle + exception UI and link to rollout steps.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: gateway-quota-enforcement feature flag updated for canary group.
telemetry-bot: FYI: created dashboards: Gateway -> Quota -> tenant rejects by route, Routing -> decision breakdown (header/ua/inferred).
